spec.cover_visual: The BrewIQ host at a navy desk at night, holding up a phone whose glowing answer bubble is being inspected through a floating holographic magnifying lens
spec.save_reason: People reuse these prompts every time an AI answer matters, like health, money or school.
spec.share_reason: Easy to send to a parent or friend who trusts chatbot answers a little too quickly.

items.title: Find the weak spots
items.benefit: See which claims in an answer need checking
items.prompt: Here is an answer an AI gave me: [PASTE ANSWER]. List every factual claim in it as a numbered list. For each claim, say how confident you are, what would prove it wrong, and what kind of source I should check.

items.title: Ask for real sources
items.benefit: Get sources you can open and read yourself
items.prompt: For the claim [CLAIM], give me up to three sources I can open myself: name, publisher, date and what each one says. If you aren't sure a source exists, say so instead of guessing.

items.title: Spot the missing context
items.benefit: Catch answers that are true but misleading
items.prompt: My question was [QUESTION]. What important context, exceptions or recent changes might your answer leave out? Tell me which ones would change the advice for someone in [MY SITUATION].

items.title: Argue the other side
items.benefit: Hear the strongest honest case against the answer
items.prompt: Take the opposite position to this answer: [PASTE ANSWER]. Give the strongest honest counter-argument, then tell me which side the evidence supports better and why.

items.title: Check the numbers
items.benefit: Catch math and unit mistakes before they cost you
items.prompt: Recalculate every number in this answer step by step: [PASTE ANSWER]. Show your working, flag any figure you can't verify, and tell me whether the conclusion still holds.

items.title: Turn it into questions
items.benefit: Walk into an appointment with the right questions
items.prompt: Based on this answer about [TOPIC], write five short questions I should ask a [PROFESSIONAL] to confirm it applies to me. Keep them plain and specific.

slides.image_prompt: CHARACTER LOCK — the BrewIQ host: the man in the reference image, about 30, warm light-brown South Asian skin, short dark wavy hair, dark brown eyes, strong dark eyebrows, light stubble, friendly confident half-smile; plain black quilted jacket with no logo or brand mark; no glasses. Identical face, hair, outfit and proportions to the reference image; never change clothing or colors; natural weight and follow-through in every movement. BRAND LOOK — rich, detailed 3D environment with cinematic lighting: midnight-navy (#0B1020) shadows, electric-cyan (#13D8E8) and vibrant-blue (#4169FF) rim and practical lights, warm-amber (#FFB547) accents, clean-white (#F6F8FC) highlights, subtle depth of field. Animated holographic 3D elements may glow and move but never contain text, letters or symbols. No beige or flat backgrounds, no slides, no floating text cards. COVER — The BrewIQ host at a navy desk at night, holding up a phone whose glowing answer bubble is being inspected through a floating holographic magnifying lens. 4:5 vertical still, the host in the lower half, clean negative space in the top 35% for the headline. No readable text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere.
